newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks retreat from highs, NYSE lifts curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks retreat from highs, NYSE lifts curbs.

text.p: Wall Street shares pulled back from session highs early Tuesday afternoon and activity slowed in somewhat cautious trade ahead of Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress on the economy.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which had hit an intraday high of 7981, drifted back to trade up 24 points at about 7931. The New York Stock Exchange lifted its curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
The Nasdaq composite was also off highs, up eight points at 1544. The long bond was up 10/32 to yield 6.52 percent.

"We had a great day this morning -- great volume and orders," Jay Meagrow, an institutional trader at McDonald & Co, said. "Things are quieting down now and volume has slowed. Nobody is canceling orders but there's no reason to be aggressive until the outcome of the Greenspan testimony."
Greenspan will deliver his mandatory, semiannual testimony on the economy and monetary policy to Congress starting at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT.
